title: The 15-Minute Sweet Potato Casserole (Skip the 1-Hour Bake)
description: Skip the hour-long bake! Make this quick 15-minute sweet potato casserole with a buttery pecan crunch topping right in your cozy kitchen.
story: I stared at my laptop until 7 PM last Tuesday, listening to the radiator clank in my tiny apartment while my stomach staged a full-scale mutiny. Ordering takeout felt financially irresponsible, and the thought of waiting an hour for a traditional holiday sweet potato casserole to bake made me want to cry into my Kerrygold butter stash. That is when I threw out the rulebook. I microwaved my yams, mashed them straight in a skillet, and topped them with a fast Trader Joe's pecan crunch. Dinner was saved in under fifteen minutes, and honestly? It tasted just as cozy as the time-consuming version without the dish-washing nightmare.
ingredients: 3 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed small so they microwave fast
1 cup mini marshmallows (optional, but heavily encouraged)
instructions: Step 1: Place your cubed sweet potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave on high for 6 to 8 minutes until fork-tender.
Step 2: Dump the tender potatoes into a skillet over medium heat. Mash them up with 2 tablespoons of butter, milk, cinnamon, and kosher salt until smooth and steaming.
Step 3: In a small bowl, mix the chopped pecans, brown sugar, and the remaining 1 tablespoon of melted butter together for your quick streusel crunch.
Step 4: Scatter the pecan topping and mini marshmallows over the warm mashed sweet potatoes. Pop the skillet under your oven broiler for 2 minutes until the marshmallows turn golden brown and gooey.
proHack: The first time I tested this, I burned the pecan topping because I walked away to answer an email. Stay right by the broiler! It takes literally 90 seconds to go from pale to perfectly toasted.
storage: Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat individual portions in the microwave for 45 seconds, though note the pecan crunch loses a bit of its snap.

faqs.question: Can I substitute maple syrup for the brown sugar?
faqs.answer: Totally! If you run out of brown sugar, use 2 tablespoons of pure maple syrup in the sweet potato mash, but stick to dry sugar for the pecan topping so it actually gets crunchy.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the sweet potato mash from getting watery?
faqs.answer: Make sure you drain any excess water after microwaving the cubed potatoes, and don't add too much milk. Start with just 2 tablespoons and add more only if needed.
